passages.text: When Simon heard this, he ground his teeth in anger and went away silently. Since a considerable part of the day still remained, Peter laid hands on the large crowd for healing and dismissed them, then went indoors with his closest companions and sat down. One of the followers, named Sophonias, said, “Blessed, Peter, is the God who chose you and filled you with wisdom for the sake of those of good judgment. For you truly discussed with Simon impressively and without resentment. We ask you also to discuss evil things with us, hoping you will disclose the account concerning him more candidly to us—and not at this very hour, but tomorrow, if you please. For we make allowance for your weariness from the inquiry.” Peter said, “I want you to know that someone who does something with pleasure is refreshed by the very exertions, whereas someone who does not do what he wishes is greatly wearied by the rest itself. So you grant me great rest by making me discuss what I enjoy.” Yet, content with his willingness and making allowance for his exertions, we asked that the postponement be until night, as was his custom, for speech to be directed to the [γνησι.....]. And, having partaken of salt, to sleep [........πημεν].

lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected text has a plural, while the following περὶ αὐτοῦ is singular. “About evil people” or “evil ones” is an alternative for the plural; the main text retains that plural-to-singular shift rather than silently regularizing both to “the evil one.”
The comparative can mean more genuinely, sincerely, or intimately. The context requests a fuller disclosure to close associates, not a claim that Peter’s prior argument was false.
The adverb conveys patient endurance of ill-treatment. “Forbearingly” is a concise alternative, less accessible in modern English.

The main text relates the temporal phrase to the requested postponement. Another attachment lets it describe making allowance for his exertions into the night; the surrounding account of his custom supports night as the deferred discussion time.

source_issues.issue: The five-dot gap after γνησι is preserved literally. The surviving πρὸς τοὺς is translated as “to the” and the surviving λέγεσθαι is taken passively as speech being directed or spoken. The stem γνησι points toward genuineness or close association, but its completion is not supplied. Missing wording could affect the infinitive’s construction or even contain a lost compound prefix, so “to converse with the ...” is a contextual alternative, not a recovered reading. The main text nominalizes the surviving speaking verb as “speech” to give readable English without inventing the content of speech. No lost words have been recovered.

The eight-dot gap and surviving ending πημεν are retained as [........πημεν] after “to sleep.” A conventional narrative formula could suggest a verb such as “turned,” but it is not restored from analogy or another passage.
